clue.text: Listen: it's impossible with this!

definitions.meaning: the command to pay attention, which also hides the anagram idea of the word rearranged
read cryptically: the word Listen given a treatment (rearranged) is impossible to hear, yet it is also the refusal to speak that makes listening pointless

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to someone who simply will not hear what is being said.
explanation.walkthrough: LISTEN given a treatment becomes SILENT, and SILENT TREATMENT, the sulky refusal to speak, leaves nothing to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the silent treatment means refusing to talk to them, so there is nothing for them to hear.

clue.text: In care?

definitions.meaning: read as 'at home', i.e. in the house rather than out
the social-services sense of looking after someone who needs help

explanation.walkthrough: 'In care' suggests a child taken into local authority care; read as 'care at home', it is domestic help for the elderly or ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A home help is a person employed, often by a council, to do housework and look after someone in their own house.

clue.text: Gone wild over Villa referee claims

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upwards, so the captured letters are read back to front
the words Villa referee claim, that is hold inside them, the run of letters needed

parts.note: the end of Villa and the start of referee

explanation.surface: A football fan complains that the referee in an Aston Villa match has lost control.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral animal is one that has escaped domestication and become wild again.

clue.text: Not that bothered about Troy's tattoos, I'd say

indicators.note: the shrug-word goes around the weight abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: meh is the slang shrug of indifference
t is the abbreviation for troy (the weight system)
to tattoo is to ink, so tattoos is inks

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a man called Troy is quite relaxed about his body art.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy looks like a man's name but stands for troy weight, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: Methinks is an old-fashioned way of saying 'it seems to me', a hedged opinion.

clue.text: Something wrong in government desire to squash left

indicators.note: the letter for left is squashed in between the other two pieces

parts.note: an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A government's urge to suppress the political left is described as a fault in the system.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor malfunction or fault, especially in machinery or software.

clue.text: Sting to appear heartless — cocky type

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain

indicators.note: the word for appear loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: to arise is to come into view

explanation.surface: Advice that the singer Sting should seem callous, followed by a dig at an arrogant sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the musician; here it is the verb meaning hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart-arse is British slang for an irritating know-all who is pleased with their own cleverness.

clue.text: Bad feeling in country church

parts.note: Mali is a West African country
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Ill will has arisen within a nation's church.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm others, a spiteful hostility.

clue.text: Bubbly Tess, nice and amorous — that's good to hear!

indicators.note: the letters fizz about like bubbles, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful, lovable woman called Tess is a delight to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubbly reads as a description of Tess but signals the rearrangement; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Music to one's ears is an idiom for news that is very welcome.

clue.text: Ponies lone wolf disturbed all at the same time

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solitary wolf panics a herd of ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: In one fell swoop is an idiom for doing everything in a single sudden action.

clue.text: Andrew initially involved with chit after money — what might the Queen say?

indicators.note: the rest follows the money letter
the initial is wrapped up inside the note of debt

parts.note: an IOU is a written note of debt

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Andrew is used

parts.note: the name supplies only its first letter here

explanation.surface: Prince Andrew caught up in some financial scandal, and the monarch's likely reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is also a female cat, so her remark is a cat's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaou is a spelling of the mewing sound a cat makes, and a queen is a female cat.

clue.text: Hole used to be hard? Rubbish!

parts.note: an eye is a small hole, as in a needle
was is the past of is
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the claim that a hole was once difficult, dismissing it as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Not sure car's meeting time limits

indicators.note: the two pieces meet the time letter, which is placed in front of them

parts.note: er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: Someone is doubtful a car will keep to its appointment deadlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini, plural of terminus, are end points or boundaries.

clue.text: He's in bother over this fellow

indicators.note: the pronoun sits inside the word for fuss

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss
the pronoun he; the 's is just 'is'
re means about, as in argue over a matter

explanation.surface: A man is in trouble because of some other man.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore is a man's given name, so a fellow could be called it.

clue.text: Drinking, right, but remaining vigilant

parts.note: on the ale means out drinking beer

explanation.surface: Someone who has been drinking claims to be still sharp and watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the alert means watchful and ready for danger.

clue.text: Picked up two words to do with roulette, which I detest

indicators.note: picked up by ear, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.words: two words to do with roulette
parts.note: bet and noir (black, one of the colours on the wheel)

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to hating a couple of gambling terms they overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: Noir is the French for black, one of the two colours at roulette.
explanation.definitionFit: A bête noire is a person or thing one particularly dislikes, literally a black beast.

clue.text: Artist supports Blades

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
piers are pillars holding up a structure

explanation.surface: A painter backs the Sheffield United football team, nicknamed the Blades.
explanation.walkthrough: Blades is the nickname of Sheffield United, but here it means swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapiers are slender thrusting swords, a kind of blade.

clue.text: President's affirmation in code

parts.note: Bush, the name of two US presidents
I do, the vow said at a wedding

explanation.surface: A US president gives his assent in some secret cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai's code of honour and conduct.

clue.text: Outlaw's sweetheart stealing granny's cash?

indicators.note: the outlaw and sweetheart together take the knot into their midst

parts.note: to ban is to outlaw
the heart of sweet is its middle letter
a granny is a kind of knot

explanation.surface: A bandit's girlfriend robs an old lady of her money.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny knot is a badly tied reef knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is paper money, so it is one form of cash; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: So can be separated from transplanted lobelias

indicators.note: the flowers are moved about like plants in a bed, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the flower name, taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that lobelias can be divided when moved to a new bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolable means capable of being isolated or set apart from others.

clue.text: School leaver, when claiming benefit, gets not much money

indicators.note: the word for when takes the benefit inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the dole is unemployment benefit
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: A teenager leaving school signs on for benefit and gets very little.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaving school is typically a teenager, an adolescent.

clue.text: Fancy discourse about name

indicators.note: the speaking word goes round the name letter

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a speech

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth about what a person is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, the adjective sense of fancy.

clue.text: Is unable to go to Glasgow for shelter

indicators.note: the phrase as a Glaswegian would say it, cannae pee

parts.note: cannae is Scots for cannot, and to go is to pee

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot travel to Glasgow looks for a roof instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like travel but is the euphemism for urinating; in Glasgow 'can't pee' is 'cannae pee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is a covering overhead giving protection from sun or rain.

clue.text: See 13
See 9
Battle over working when it's raining hard

parts.note: Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
on, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A sporting contest continues despite heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The monsoon is the rainy season in South Asia, a period of torrential downpours.

clue.text: Fresh scandal, might you say, in old lock-up

parts.note: new means fresh
-gate, after Watergate, is tagged on to name any scandal, hence 'might you say'

explanation.surface: A new scandal breaks at a former prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a historic London jail, so it is a former place of confinement.

clue.text: American mineral water in Barking but not Washington!

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the remaining letters go crazy
the letters of Washington are removed

parts.note: these two words taken as written, before the state letters are removed
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A US mineral water is on sale in Barking, east London, but not in the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the London suburb, but it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Niter is the American spelling of nitre, saltpetre, a naturally occurring mineral.

clue.text: Flipping work! Drudge penning book, which should pay the bills

indicators.note: flipped over, so the word for work is turned back to front

parts.note: op, short for opus

indicators.note: the drudge encloses the book letter

parts.note: a toiler is a hard worker

explanation.surface: An exasperated hack labours over a book written purely for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse but signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a work produced quickly just to earn a living, to keep the pot boiling.
